source_text: eiusque partes quibus constat, non immerito vobis Christianorum infensissima multitudo, singillatim describendo et deridendo percurris, in quibus et "auditoriales scholasticos" tangis, et dicis contra me clamaturos: "O tempora, o mores!" [n94] et tamen vulgi iudicium reformidas, ubi tam clamosos tibi suffragatores invenire potuisti, qui Tullianis me vocibus territent; quod "aliunde quam unde totum est, esse putem genitalem corporis partem".
pass_a_gloss: And its parts of which it consists, the multitude of Christians not undeservedly most hostile to you (plural), by describing and deriding one by one you run through, among which you touch also 'lecture-hall scholars', and you say (they are) going to cry out against me: 'O times, O customs!' And yet the judgement of the crowd you dread, where such clamorous supporters for you you were able to find, who would terrify me with Tullian voices; because 'from elsewhere than whence the whole is, I think the genital part of the body to be'.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “You run through the parts that make up the people (the multitude of Christians, which with good reason is most hostile to you), describing and mocking them one by one; among them you touch on ‘the students who attend lectures,’ and you say that they will shout against me: ‘O the times, O the morals!’ (Cicero, Against Catiline 1) And yet you dread the verdict of the crowd, where you could find supporters so loud for you that they would frighten me with Tullius’s words, because ‘I think that the genital part of the body comes from somewhere other than where the whole comes from.’”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
